Anna —

Thanks for the clear asks and the workbook — useful baseline. I skimmed the attachment and sketched a pragmatic approach below that balances latency targets and cost predictability. I copied Planning and Sales ops so we can commit to a mutual action plan and procurement cadence.

Proposed tiered plan (initial):
- APAC pilot (SG): 6 dedicated nodes (A100-equivalent), 1 standby burst tranche (2 nodes) for peak events — estimated sustained throughput ~260 qps with prefix caching.
- EU steady-state (Ireland): 4 dedicated nodes to meet 100 qps with room to auto-scale to 6 for holiday peaks.
- US buffer (us-central): 2 hot standby nodes routed for failover + cheaper cold pool for large backfills.

Notes:
- This assumes quantization to 4-bit on the heavier model variant (recommended in the workbook) and prefix KV caching for the assistant workload.
- We recommend a 3-month pilot SLA (best-effort latency SLO) with an optional Dedicated upgrade to SLA-backed commitment if Helio hits Tier A deal triggers.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Planning (Irene) to validate node counts and run a quick cost delta for 6->8 APAC nodes.
2) Sales ops (Ben) to map these to an initial 3‑month committed price and list the scalable burst options.
3) Karthik to draft routing and failover policy text for the contract.

Irene / Ben / Karthik — can you each take an action below and I will consolidate for Anna and procurement by Friday?

—David
